feedback: Written before this candidate races. Race 4 (entityR2A, 578.99) is the best result and shows that the y = 0.06 lead fixed oval (20 of 20) and improved s-bend (13 of 20), with s-bend line loss at 0.55. Slalom still lost the line at 1.1 per run with max_error at the 0.06 m limit, and race 3 (entityR2B, 235.88) shows that widening to 0.04 m did not fix that failure, so the spread is not the limiter. Race 4 moved the lead from 0.05 to 0.06 and cut oval oscillation only from 0.311 to 0.302, so the lead is a weak lever for oscillation. The next race should therefore test controller gain and speed, not geometry. Your 7-sensor coverage idea is untested in races, so treat it as exploration, to be tried only if slalom still fails. Once the race reports, use this rule. If slalom line loss falls below 1 and some slalom finishes appear, keep the geometry as it is. If slalom line loss stays at 1 or more with max_error at the limit, I will tune kp and base_speed first. If that still fails, the next geometry candidate is the 7-sensor layout at x = -0.03 to +0.03 (about 10 mm pitch) with 16 mm footprints and y = 0.06, which adds coverage without widening the spread. Keep y at 0.06 unless oval finishes fall below about 18 of 20.
requested_changes: Hold the race 4 geometry unchanged for the next race (±0.03 m spread, 16 mm footprints, y = 0.06, 0.8 kg, 12 cm body and track, 3 cm wheels), so the controller change is tested alone against race 4.

If slalom line loss stays at 1 or more with max_error at 0.06 after controller tuning, try seven 16 mm sensors at x = -0.03, -0.02, -0.01, 0, 0.01, 0.02, 0.03 with y = 0.06 as the next geometry test. Expect the sensor_weights and kp to be rescaled by the Integrator.

Do not move the lead further forward (y 0.065 to 0.07) unless oval steering_oscillation stays above 0.25 and oval finishes hold at 18 or more of 20. Race 4 showed the lead move from 0.05 to 0.06 changed oscillation by only about 0.01.
